intro: Philadelphia listings advertise non-climate 10x10 units from about $63, while typical street rates run about $136–$140/month. The city is tight on storage — about 3.5 square feet per person — so the number on the banner is a poor guide. Once the move-in special ends and the first existing-customer increase lands, the six-month average sits well above the advertised rate.

units.notes: Locker / closet size. Fixed fees dominate the true cost at this size. Non-climate listings from about $20; climate-controlled web specials from about $5. Climate-controlled street rate ~$62.
Walk-in closet; studio overflow. No reliable lowest-promo figure published for this size (gap). Climate-controlled ~$100.

Most rented size. City average $136, down 1.5% YoY (StorageCafe, Sep 2026) and $136, down 2.9% YoY (StorageUnitCosts, Aug 2026). Philadelphia metro averages $140, down 3.2% YoY (Storage Stats). Climate-controlled ~$149. Non-climate listings from about $63; some climate promos from $15.
Two-bedroom contents. Estimate: single source (StorageCafe, Sep 2026). Climate-controlled ~$194.
Three-bedroom home or a car. Climate-controlled ~$244. Non-climate listings from about $125; some climate promos from $25.

local_tips: StorageCafe lists Parkwood (~$91), Olney (~$95) and Allegheny West (~$107) among the cheapest areas for a standard unit, while Northeast Philadelphia Airport (~$384) and Logan Square (~$244) run highest.
Philadelphia's all-unit average is lowest around December (~$154) and highest in June and July (~$160), StorageCafe. The swing is modest; the promo terms matter more than the month.
Only about 112,000 sq ft of new storage is due in 2026, down 46% from last year (StorageCafe), and the city has roughly 3.5 sq ft per person — less room to shop around than in a Sun Belt market.
Extra Space charges a $50 admin fee (per StorageUnitCosts), higher than our $29 default; adjust the calculator if your facility charges more.
